sheet-2-1.description: The main part of sheet 2 shows the bay front of Keansburg at New Point Comfort, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It is bounded by Raritan Bay on the north and west, Highland Avenue on the east and Highland Boulevard on the south, with the block corner of Pine Wood Place at the lower left. The upper half is the resort and amusement district along the board walk: the New Point Comfort Steamboat Pier, 1200 feet long, leaves the shore at the top left, with a restaurant built on piles beside it; a row of small shops and stands lines the board walk, and behind it are a skating rink with billiards, a lunch stand, a circle marked for sea planes, the Jack Rabbit roller coaster and a figure-eight ride beside Ye Old Mill, a shooting gallery and a fish pier. South of New Point Comfort Beachway are Camp Raritan with a summer hotel and restaurant, an open-air structure, and a large cement-floored garage. The lower half is residential: Bay Avenue, Sea Breeze Way and Highland Boulevard run east to Highland Avenue, while their western ends turn diagonally along the shore, with a board walk following the bay edge. The blocks there are laid out in narrow lots with scattered frame dwellings and bungalows, several named (Wolf Den, Sand Bank, Bonnie Jean, The Wesley, The Belmont). An eight-inch water pipe runs along New Point Comfort Beachway and three-inch pipes along Bay Avenue, Sea Breeze Way and Highland Boulevard. A separate inset at the top left, cut off by a heavy line, shows part of Ideal Beach at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: The board walk along the shore at the lower left is now Beachway Avenue; New Point Comfort Beachway is also Beachway Avenue today.
Sea Breeze Way is now Seabreeze Way; Pine Wood Place is now Pinewood Place.
The New Point Comfort Steamboat Pier is labelled 1200 feet long.
Amusements drawn include the Jack Rabbit coaster, a figure-eight ride, Ye Old Mill and a skating rink.

50 ft (main part): the bay front at New Point Comfort, boardwalk, Bay Av, Sea Breeze Way, Pine Wood Pl, Highland Blvd, Highland Av, piers. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 inset at top left (100 ft): Ideal Beach east end, Bayview Av, Sea Breeze Av, Beachway, Port Monmouth & Keansburg Rd.

sheet-2-2.description: The inset in the upper left corner of sheet 2, cut off from the main map by a heavy line, shows the eastern end of Ideal Beach at 100 feet to an inch, with its own scale note and a north arrow pointing to the upper left. It lies east of Bay View Avenue, where sheet 15 adjoins, between Raritan Bay on the north and the Port Monmouth and Keansburg Road on the south. Bayside Parkway runs along the shore past a wooden pier at the top, and Beachway runs through the middle of the inset parallel to the road. Sea Breeze Avenue ends at Bay View Avenue on the left. The blocks numbered 275, 282, 400 and 401 are cut into narrow lots, almost all empty: block 401 holds an open arena with a row of small dwellings, a frame building with a power house supplying power and light, a gasoline station and a few dwellings near the road. A wide empty strip separates the inset from the beach front of New Point Comfort on the main map.
notes: Placed from two junctions carried from sheet 15 (Bay View Avenue at Sea Breeze Avenue and at the road), with the scale and the rotation of sheet 15; low confidence.
Bay View Avenue lies near today's Williams Avenue line; Beachway and the shore end of Bayside Parkway east of it no longer exist as streets.

50 ft (main part): the bay front at New Point Comfort, boardwalk, Bay Av, Sea Breeze Way, Pine Wood Pl, Highland Blvd, Highland Av, piers. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 inset at top left (100 ft): Ideal Beach east end, Bayview Av, Sea Breeze Av, Beachway, Port Monmouth & Keansburg Rd.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the New Point Comfort amusement and summer-boarding district of Keansburg on the shore of Raritan Bay, at 50 feet to an inch. The map is bounded by the bay and the Board Walk at the upper right and by Highland Avenue, Center and Grand View Avenue at the left and bottom. At the top left, along the Board Walk, stand the resort's attractions: a large Carousel, the New Plaza Hotel and restaurant, a row of small stands and a photographer's, and a hollow-tile building housing a restaurant and drug store. Offshore, yellow strips mark the bathing piers running into the bay, and a circular ride called The Whip stands at the shore. Below the Board Walk, the blocks between Highland Avenue, Carr Avenue and Raritan Avenue are filled with moving-picture theatres (one with a stage, marked no heat, lights gas and electric), restaurants, lunch rooms, a bakery, hardware, groceries, the College Inn, the Washington House, The Delaware, Hartford Cottage, St Albans, The Poplars and many summer boarding houses with small dwellings and tents. New Point Comfort Beachway runs diagonally along the shore, with Holland House, East View House and Sea View Ho. on its inner side. East of Raritan Avenue the diagonal Fair View Avenue and Grand View Avenue enclose long narrow lots with cottages and boarding houses such as The Savoy, The Laurel, Elizabeth Edna and The Sea Breeze, some with tents. Water pipes of 3 and 8 inches are shown in the streets. The left and bottom edges are cut by the adjoining sheets 2, 5 and 4.
notes: Highland Boulevard is lettered with abbreviations (B'LV'D) on the sheet.
Sea Breeze Way is Seabreeze Way today and New Point Comfort Beachway (with the Board Walk) is now Beachway Avenue.
Fair View Avenue and Grand View Avenue are not in the OpenStreetMap extract under those names and were not used as control.
Center Avenue and its junctions with Carr and Raritan Avenues lie on the bottom edge of the sheet and were not detected.
Water pipe sizes lettered in the streets are 3 inch and 8 inch.
50 ft. Board Walk / New Point Comfort Beachway amusements, Bay, Highland, Carr and Raritan Avs; Fair View and Grand View Av diagonal blocks east (not in OSM, east part uncontrolled).

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the middle of Keansburg's summer-resort district between the Raritan Bay shore and Center Avenue, at 50 feet to an inch, with the blocks south of Center Avenue as far as Raritan and Carr Avenues. The upper two thirds of the sheet is a regular grid: New Point Comfort Beachway and the Board Walk run along the top edge, and Grand View, Belleview, Ocean View, Sea View and Bay View Avenues run down the page to Center Avenue, enclosing long narrow lots that are numbered along the avenues. Almost every lot holds a small dwelling or a named summer boarding house or bungalow, among them Wesemans Beach Villa, the Bay Side, Koehlers Villa, Greenwich Villa, the Massachusetts, the Waverly, Philips Ho, the White Ho, the Navajo and the Colonial, with a concrete tennis court near the top right. Hollow-tile buildings (Arbor Vitae, Point Comfort and a small one near Ocean View Avenue) stand near the shore end of the blocks. A compass rose with a north arrow set at an angle stands at the top. South of Center Avenue the street plan turns: Raritan Avenue, Fox Avenue, Oak Avenue, East Shore and Carr Avenue run diagonally, and the narrow lots along them hold cottages, boarding houses and a few shops, including a restaurant on Carr Avenue and the Dew Drop Inn. Large blocks numbered 28 to 31 and 16, 17, 21 and 22 are marked. The adjoining sheets are 3 at the left, 5 below and 6 at the right, and the sheet number references 5 and 6 appear along its margins. Water pipes of 3 and 8 inches are drawn in the streets.
notes: Belleview Avenue is spelled Belleview on the sheet and in OpenStreetMap; Ocean View, Sea View and Bay View Avenues are now Oceanview Avenue, Seaview Avenue and Bayview Avenue.
Oak Avenue is now Oak Street, East Shore is now East Shore Street, and New Point Comfort Beachway and the Board Walk are now Beachway Avenue.
Grand View Avenue is not in the OpenStreetMap extract and was not used as control.
Center Avenue is drawn 50 feet wide, narrower than its modern parcel width, so a drawn width was set for it in the config.
The junction of Bay View Avenue and Center Avenue lies at the right edge of the sheet and was not detected.
50 ft. Grand View to Bay View Avs grid above Center Av; diagonal Raritan/Fox/Oak/Carr/East Shore blocks below, turned about 39 degrees.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the west side of the Keansburg resort district at 50 feet to an inch, from Highland Boulevard at the top to West Shore, South and Gillett Streets at the bottom and from North Shore at the left to Carr Avenue and Raritan Avenue at the right. A compass rose and north arrow stand at the upper right. Along the top, Highland Boulevard is lined with summer boarding houses and cottages (Hunters Roost, The Rosamond, Roseville Cottage, the Melrose hotel, Highland Ho and The Elitz), and the long lots between Highland Boulevard and Center hold small dwellings, a bathhouse and a restaurant. At the left the Keansburg Water Works stand pipe, with its capacity noted, and the tract of Washington Heights are drawn. Below Center, the block numbered 14 holds The Fliver and The Clinton among a row of small cottages. The large irregular block at the right, numbered 15, is Camp Jahns Association, a tent and cottage colony with a club house, dining room and kitchen, sleeping rooms and a platform, enclosed by dashed lines. Walter and Jahn Streets run diagonally through narrow lots of cottages and boarding houses such as Crowd Inn, The Dally and Carlow. At the centre, between Oak Street and Jahn Street, the Keansburg Water Works pumping station with its filter basins is described in a long legend, next to the New Point Comfort Fire Department. South of Oak the lots toward West Shore are largely open, with Camp Lucilla at the far left, and a National Camp, restaurants and a bakery at the lower right near Carr and Raritan Avenues. The fan of lots at the left edge belongs to the adjoining sheet 8.
notes: Highland Blvd is lettered Highland BLVD on the sheet; it is Highland Boulevard today.

Walter is now Walters Street; N. Shore and W. Shore are now North Shore Street and West Shore Street; Oak is now Oak Street; Gillett is now Gillette Street; Saint Marks Avenue is now Saint Marks Place.
Pinewood Place and the junction of Highland Boulevard with it are on the top edge of the sheet and were not detected.
The Keansburg Water Works legend gives pump and basin capacities in gallons.
50 ft. Highland Blvd to West Shore, Camp Jahns Association, water works pumping station; turned about 35 degrees.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 is a 100-feet-to-an-inch map of the central and eastern part of Keansburg, running from the Raritan Bay shore and Board Walk at the top to Carr Avenue and the Seeley Avenue and Maple Avenue district at the bottom, and from Bay View Avenue and Pine View Avenue at the left to Woodland, Johnson Lane and Forest Avenue at the right. A compass rose and north arrow stand at the upper left, and the bay and yellow bathing piers cross the top. Along the Board Walk are rows of numbered bungalows (Sheehan Bungalows), a dance hall and, at the upper middle, bath houses, a restaurant and a pavilion. The lots between New Point Comfort Beachway, Camp View Place and Bay View Avenue, numbered 147, 148 and 149, are filled with small summer cottages, many with names such as Hotel Patsy, Rose Cottage, Irene, Thelma and Rose. Eastward, St. Johns Park and St. Johns Summer Boarding lie along Shore Boulevard, with a dense cluster of small bungalows and shacks near Main Street; Ocean Boulevard and Charlevoix Place run along the upper right. Main Street and Collins Street run diagonally to a junction near the centre, where Seeley Avenue and Forest Avenue lead away. The south and east are sparsely built: large unplatted tracts (46A, 46C, 264) hold only scattered dwellings, with Mapplewood, Vincent Ho and Wakeya near Locust Street and Commodore Avenue. Raritan Avenue and the Seeley Avenue blocks at the lower left continue onto sheets 4, 5 and 8, and Carr Avenue crosses the bottom. The sheet number references 4, 5, 8, 9, 10 and 13 appear in the margins.
notes: Bay View, Pine View and Camp View Avenues are now Bayview Avenue, Pine View Avenue and Camp View Avenue; Camp View Place and Shore Boulevard keep their names.
East Shore is now East Shore Street; Locust is Locust Street; Main is Main Street; New Point Comfort Beachway is Beachway Avenue; Lincoln Ter. is now Lincoln Court.
The Brookside Avenue, Collins Street, Pine View Avenue and Seeley Avenue junction near the lower left lies about 5 m from where the sheet draws it and was not used as control.
Sheet 6 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch; scale notes appear at the top and bottom.
100 ft. Central district, Bay View to Forest Av, Shore Blvd, Johnson Lane, Pine View, Collins, Grove; one part.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 shows West Keansburg at 100 feet to an inch, the area west of Waackaack Creek between Raritan Bay and 7th Street. At the top, Bay Avenue runs along the bay shore past the mouth of Waackaack Creek, and across the creek to the northeast are Charles Avenue, Maplewood Avenue and Creek Road with a small group of dwellings and stores, one of them of hollow tile. Laurel Avenue crosses the creek on a steel bridge and runs south down the middle of the sheet. West of it is a regular grid of long blocks numbered 204 to 220, bounded by Park Avenue on the west and crossed by a street marked not named, then 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th and 7th Streets, with Central Avenue through the middle. The blocks are divided into narrow lots and are almost all empty in 1923: only scattered one and one-and-a-half storey frame dwellings, a few hollow tile buildings and sheds. Thornes Creek runs down the west edge and a branch of it crosses the lower left corner, where block 219 is marked swamp. The Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the lower part of the sheet between 5th and 6th Streets. East of Laurel Avenue, the large tracts 216, 217, 218 and 395 have a few dwellings along unnamed streets that continue on sheet 11.
notes: Park Avenue is now North Park Avenue north of the railroad and South Park Avenue south of it.
The Central Railroad of New Jersey line is abandoned.
Junctions on 1st Street were rejected at about 11 m and 7th Street / Central Avenue at 25 m; the modern streets may not follow the 1923 lines there.
Laurel Avenue crosses Waackaack Creek on a steel bridge.
A street is lettered "Not Named" on the sheet.
100 ft. West Keansburg (Hazlet): Bay Av, Riverside, Charles, numbered streets First to Seventh, Park Av, Waackaack Creek, Thorns Creek, railroad.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 is a 100-feet-to-an-inch map of the west side of Keansburg, from the Raritan Bay shore at the top to Washington Avenue at the bottom, and from Waackaack Creek at the left to Pinewood Place, North Shore and Carr Avenue at the right. At the top, the Belvidere Beach Amusement Co. Inc. (P. Licardi, owner) occupies a large tract on Bay Avenue with refreshment stands, The Doggem, a dance hall with storage, a bath house and a concrete swimming pool on the shore, and a row of bungalows along Bay Avenue. Below it, blocks 117 and 118 between Sea Breeze Way and Highland Boulevard hold narrow lots with cottages and boarding houses such as the Mansion House, Pine Lodge, Keystone Cottage, the Sorrento, Sun Rise, Beach Haven and Bericare. Hotel Mahler stands at the left on Laurel Avenue. The middle of the sheet is a mixed district of cottages along Maplewood Avenue, Saint Peters Avenue, Saint Mark's Avenue and Seeley Avenue, with The Loch Lomond, Marion Hanover, Belvedere Inn and Windsor, and block numbers 115, 116, 119 and 120. A hollow-tile building and a reservoir with pump and water tank stand near Highland Boulevard. Waackaack Creek winds down the left side, and along Creek Road (also called Waackaack Avenue) are blocks 191, 193 and 194 with Murry Lane, Willow, Howard Avenue and Rowland Street. The lower right, around Lincoln, Ramsay, Garfield and Myrtle Avenues, has lots in blocks 121 to 130 with a few boarding houses, and Carr Avenue runs diagonally along the right edge. The adjoining sheets are 2, 5, 6, 7 and 9.
notes: Sea Breeze Way is now Seabreeze Way; Ramsay Avenue is now Ramsey Avenue; Rowland Street is now Roland Street; Murry Lane is now Murray Lane; Gillett is now Gillette Street.
Creek Road (Waackaack Avenue) is Creek Road today; Saint James Avenue, Saint Mark's Avenue and Saint Peters Avenue are now Saint James Place, Saint Marks Place and Saint Peters Place.
Highland Boulevard is lettered with abbreviations (B'LV'D) on the sheet.
The Sea Breeze Way junctions at Oakwood Place and Pinewood Place sit about 4.5 m from the fitted position and may be drawn off the modern street line.
Howard Avenue and Creek Road junctions with Murry Lane were rejected as 9 to 11 m off.
100 ft. West side of Keansburg, Belvidere Beach amusements to Washington Av, Waackaack Creek at left; one part.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the central part of Keansburg south of the bay front, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It runs from Washington Place and Washington Avenue at the top down to Church Street at the bottom, and from Creek Road (Waackaack Avenue) and Waackaack Creek on the west to Main Street and Lincoln Terrace on the east. The middle of the sheet is a regular grid of long narrow blocks numbered 137A to 140B between Beacon, Ramsay, Myrtle and Carr Avenues, crossed by Maple, 4th Street, Terrace Place, Frances Place and Manning Place. Most of these blocks are laid out in small lots but still empty in 1923, with only scattered frame dwellings and summer cottages, many of them named (Maple Cottage, Orchard Cottage, Harold Cottage, Four Gables). The denser southern blocks between Manning Place and Church Street hold the older Keansburg Public School, a post office, a garage, a dress and underwear factory of A. W. Wolf, drug and sundries stores, a bowling alley and dance hall, and the fire department on Frances Place near Main Street. Institutions include the newer Keansburg Public School on Frances Place, St. Ann's Roman Catholic Church and its rectory on Carr Avenue, and the 1st M. E. Church near Church Street. The U.S. Government Waackaack Light steel tower stands beside Creek Road. The Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the lower left corner next to Waackaack Creek, with a bridge carrying Tenth Street over the creek and Munro Avenue or Stone Road leaving to the south. A four-inch water pipe is drawn along Maple and down Carr Avenue and Randall Place.
notes: 4th Street is now Kennedy Way.
Beacon Avenue is now Waackaack Avenue; the Creek Road printed as Waackaack Avenue is today's Creek Road.
Ramsay Avenue is now Ramsey Avenue; Frances Place is now Francis Place; Wilson Place is now Wilson Avenue; Lincoln Terrace is now Lincoln Court.
The Central Railroad of New Jersey line across the lower left corner is abandoned.
Frances Place is marked not open between blocks 142 and 143.
100 ft. Washington Av to Church St: Fourth, Terrace, Maple, Frances, Manning, Carr Av, Myrtle, Wilson, Beacon, Hamsey.

sheet-10-1.description: The main part of sheet 10 covers the eastern side of central Keansburg at 100 feet to an inch, from Broander Place and Randolph Place at the top to below the Port Monmouth and Keansburg Road at the bottom, and from Lincoln Terrace and Main Street on the west to Forest and Twilight Avenues on the east. A heavy line along its upper right edge separates it from an inset of the Port Monmouth side. The upper left blocks along Main Street are the busiest part of the sheet: the Keansburg Auditorium, Macdonald's Raritan Bay House hotel with its summer pavilion, a bakery, groceries, meat and vegetable stores, a hardware store, a barber, a post office, a police station, a dairy and milk depot and the Entertainers Club. Small cottages and bungalows, many named (Shady Side, The Rambler, Baldwins Villa, Glen Gran), fill the blocks along Lawrence, Beachwood, Briarwood and Park Avenues. South of Park Avenue a large tract numbered 51 is almost empty except for a garage for 25 cars; at its lower corner Memorial Hall, used for moving pictures, stands on the Port Monmouth and Keansburg Road. Willis and Forest Avenues run south to that road lined with narrow lots, and the block between Crescent, Forest and Twilight Avenues is crossed by the unopened Albert Place. South of the road, Hancock Street and Hancock Place have a few dwellings and tents in the large tract 288.
notes: Beachwood Avenue is now Beechwood Avenue; Crescent is now Crescent Street; the Port Monmouth & Keansburg Road is now Port Monmouth Road.
Lawrence Avenue was left out of the control: its modern junctions lie 11 to 15 m from where the sheet draws them.
Albert Place is drawn dashed and marked arbitrary through block 165.
A dwelling south of the road is marked as drawn from plans.

100 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map (Main St, Randolph, Lawrence, Park Av, Beachwood, Briarwood, Willis, Forest, Crescent, Twilight, Port Monmouth & Keansburg Rd); part 2 inset right of the heavy line: Port Monmouth area (Prospect, Raynor, Clinton, Center, South End, Bray Avs).

sheet-10-2.description: The inset on the right of sheet 10, cut off from the main map by a heavy line, shows the eastern edge of East Keansburg toward Port Monmouth at 100 feet to an inch, with its own north arrow turned to the upper left. It covers the long diagonal blocks between Prospect Avenue, Prospect Place, Raynor Avenue, Ralph, Centre Avenue and South End Avenue, cut across by Clinton and Bray Avenues, with Eastmond Avenue at the lower right. At the upper left are Weehawken Avenue and Alpha Place where sheet 15 adjoins, and a short Linden Street beside Clinton. The blocks are laid out in narrow 25 foot lots, most of them empty; only scattered one and one-and-a-half storey frame dwellings, a few sheds and one concrete block dwelling are built. The large tracts 437 and 451 on the right are blank, with a note that there is no exposure beyond them, and Port Monmouth is lettered at the top. Sheet 16 adjoins at the lower left.
notes: Centre Avenue is now Center Avenue; Eastmond Avenue is now Eastmond Place; the Linden Street beside Clinton is near today's Laurel Place.
The inset is drawn somewhat out of square with the modern streets; its fit rests on six junctions with a leave-one-out error of about 8 m.

100 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map (Main St, Randolph, Lawrence, Park Av, Beachwood, Briarwood, Willis, Forest, Crescent, Twilight, Port Monmouth & Keansburg Rd); part 2 inset right of the heavy line: Port Monmouth area (Prospect, Raynor, Clinton, Center, South End, Bray Avs).

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 shows the southern part of West Keansburg at 100 feet to an inch, mostly a subdivision of long narrow lots with very few buildings. The plan is a fan of wide streets: Central Avenue and Holly Avenue run down the left side, and Laurel, Pinewood and Poplar Avenues cross the middle, while 7th to 13th Streets run across them, and the curved 7th and 9th Streets bend along the upper right. Street widths of 45, 50 and 60 feet are lettered. A strip along 8th Street and the top is marked as the Street Railway right of way, and the Central Railroad of New Jersey passes across the top right corner. The densest built-up area is at the top: West Keansburg Public School stands on the left, small dwellings and hollow-tile houses sit near the 8th Street end, and a group of storage buildings, labelled storage of building material, lines 7th Street at the upper right. Further south almost every block is shown only as numbered lots (blocks 225 to 250), with isolated dwellings, a boarding house on Munro Avenue and a shed near 13th Street. Newman and Jersey Streets cross the right side, and Munro Avenue runs diagonally across the bottom with 13th Street. The adjoining sheet 7 lies above and the rest of the sheet's edges are blank. A compass rose and north arrow stand at the right, and the sheet is stamped May 1923 with West Keansburg lettered below the Keansburg stamp.
notes: Munro Avenue is not in the OpenStreetMap extract under that name.
Central Avenue, Holly Avenue and 7th, 9th Streets are drawn as a paper plat and did not fit the modern streets (junctions 6 to 12 m off), so they were left out of the control.
Poplar Avenue and 13th Street junctions fit about 2 to 4 m off; the fit is weak (12 points, 2.5 m RMSE) and the sheet may be drawn slightly off scale.
Jersey and Newman are drawn bare on the sheet; they are Jersey Street and Newman Street today.

100 ft. West Keansburg south (7th to 13th Sts, Central to Poplar Avs); a paper plat whose streets mostly do not follow the modern grid: Central, Holly, 7th, 9th, Newman (in part) left out; low confidence.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the southern part of central Keansburg at 100 feet to an inch, from Church Street at the top to the open land south of Leonards Lane, and from Waackaack Creek and the Munro Avenue or Stone Road corner on the west to Main Street and Hancock Street on the east. The diagonal band of the abandoned Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the upper half from the depot near Wood Avenue to the right edge, with a street railway right of way running across the sheet below it. Along the tracks stand the borough hall and jail, the depot, an express office, Keansburg Lumber and Supply Company, Collins Brothers coal yard and building materials, a lumber shed, and Conover Lumber Company beside Hancock Street. The long street drawn as Palmer Avenue runs south-south-west from the railroad crossing to the foot of the sheet and carries the frontage of most of the dwellings; Mason, Charles, Palmer and Euclid-side blocks lie east of it, and Park, Linton, Frederick, Moran, Willow, Locust and St. John Places run west from it to Leroy Place and Linden Place. Houses are mostly small frame dwellings, many named (Magdaline, Mason Villa, Cozy Haven, Gingerwood, Bell Vue, Meadow Buff), on narrow lots. Large parts of the sheet are open ground: the private-road tract around The Monmouth, Arabelle, Quinlan and Laffalot at upper left, tracts 337A, 337B and 346 along the creek, and a proposed street at lower right. The part to the right of Main Street above Hancock Street is marked as sheet 10, and a stamp of the Princeton map division sits at the lower right.
notes: Palmer Avenue on this sheet is now Main Street; Locust Avenue is now Loshen Place, Willow Avenue is now Magnolia Place and St. John Place is now St Johns Place.
Charles, Park Place and Linden Place correspond to modern Charles Street, Poplar Street and Vogel Street (Park Place and Linden Place not used as control).
Carr Avenue is also lettered Salina Pl. on the sheet.
Port Monmouth & Keansburg Road is now Port Monmouth Road; the street lettered Beach is now Beech Street and the street lettered Railroad near Carr Avenue is now Depot Street.
The Central Railroad of New Jersey is abandoned and gave no control.
Wood Avenue was left out of the control: the modern line lies about 36 m from where the sheet draws it.
A street is lettered "Proposed Street" on the sheet.
A street is lettered "Private Road" on the sheet.
A street is lettered "Driveway" on the sheet.
100 ft. Church St south: Palmer Av (now Main St), Wood St to St John Pl, Leroy Pl, Euclid Av; railroad depot and freight depot, Keansburg Lumber & Supply Co.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the northeastern part of Keansburg along Raritan Bay at 100 feet to an inch. The shoreline and the water of Raritan Bay run across the top of the sheet, with Ocean Boulevard and Shore Boulevard as the first two streets behind it. Below them lie a grid of long narrow blocks (156, 157, 158A, 158B and the tracts 381 to 389) bounded by Highland Place, Grand View Place, Lakewood Avenue and Birchwood Avenue, with Lawrence Avenue and Beacon Light Avenue running down the sheet. A dashed line lettered Middletown Township crosses the upper right, and beyond it Beacon Boulevard, Lighthouse Road and Bayside Parkway reach toward the Point Comfort Light. The upper blocks are mostly open, with scattered dwellings and a row of small cottages along Ocean Boulevard. The lower left and middle of the sheet is drawn on a different grid: Twilight Avenue, Woodside Place, Woodside Avenue, Forest Street and Lawrence run south-east in long strips of narrow lots, with curved streets (Seawood and Greenwood) at the left edge. Park Avenue, Cottage Place, Crescent, Orchard, Shadyside Avenue and Parkside Place form the denser dwelling blocks at lower right, around Forest Park, tract 162, which is left blank. A water company works stands beside Park Avenue. The abutting sheets are numbered in the margins (6 at left, 10 below, 14 at right).
notes: Ocean Boulevard and Highland Place have no street of that name in the modern data; Shore Boulevard, Lakewood, Birchwood, Woodland and Lawrence Avenues, Beacon Light Avenue and Twilight Avenue keep their names.
Orchard is now Orchard Street, Crescent is now Crescent Street, and Seawood and Greenwood are now Seawood Avenue and Greenwood Place.
The street lettered Beacon Blvd. is now Beacon Boulevard; Lighthouse Road is not in the modern street data.
Lawrence Avenue gave consistent control on this sheet (residuals 1.5 to 3 m) although it was displaced on sheet 10.
A heavy dashed line near the upper right is lettered with the township boundary, Middletown Township.
100 ft. Shore district NE: Ocean/Shore Blvd, Lakewood, Birchwood, Lawrence, Beacon Light, Twilight, Park, Crescent, Shadyside; grid turned about -35 deg.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14, titled Ideal Beach and East Keansburg, covers the shore district east of central Keansburg at 100 feet to an inch. Raritan Bay and its shoreline run across the top, with a compass rose at the upper centre; Bayside Parkway follows the shore, with a lettered walk along the water at the upper right. The sheet is divided into long blocks by Orchard, Beacon Boulevard, Morningside Avenue, Fairview Avenue and Atlantic Avenue running down the page, and by Lighthouse Road, Park Avenue, Sea Breeze, Monmouth, Raritan and Navesink Avenues running across it. The Port Monmouth and Keansburg Road crosses the lower half diagonally from the lower left to the right edge, lined with numbered lots on both sides. Housing is almost entirely small frame dwellings and cottages, many named (Bronx Villa, Orchard Villa, Sandimere, Corinthian, Brook Cottage, Le Roy), with a few stores, an auto repair shop, an auto service station and sheds along the road, a dancing pavilion and a repair shop at the upper right, and Lincoln Park as a small triangular open lot near the middle. The bottom third, south of the road, shows long narrow lots between Atlantic, Pacific and Bay Avenues, mostly unbuilt, with Neptune Place and Walling Place crossing them. Block numbers carry second numbers in parentheses (277 (102), 161 (103), 289 (104), 286 (105)), and the neighbouring sheets 13, 15 and 10 are noted at the margins.
notes: Sea Breeze Avenue is now Seabreeze Avenue; Raritan Avenue corresponds to modern Ideal Avenue; Fairview Avenue to modern Sunset Street; Orchard and Crescent are now Orchard Street and Crescent Street; Port Monmouth & Keansburg Road is now Port Monmouth Road.
The word Keansburg is lettered in spaced capitals across the lower blocks, between Atlantic and Pacific Avenues and Bay Avenue, as for a street or a place name.
Neptune Place / Pacific Avenue (14 m) and Atlantic Avenue / Port Monmouth Road (9 m) lay far from their modern nodes and were rejected.
100 ft. Ideal Beach and East Keansburg: Bayside Pkwy to Port Monmouth & Keansburg Rd, Atlantic, Pacific, Bay, Neptune Pl; Raritan Av is now Ideal Avenue.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15, also titled Ideal Beach and E. Keansburg, covers the eastern part of the shore district at 100 feet to an inch. Raritan Bay appears at the top, with the Board Parkway and Bayside Parkway running along the shore. The upper half is a regular grid of long blocks (271 to 285, with their second numbers 107 to 110 in parentheses) between Ocean, Hudson, Bray and Weehawken Avenues and the cross streets Sea Breeze, Monmouth, Raritan and Navesink Avenues; most of these lots are narrow and many are still vacant, with dwellings scattered across them and Roosevelt Park left as an open lot beside Hudson Avenue. The Port Monmouth and Keansburg Road crosses diagonally from the lower left to the upper right, lined with numbered lots, stores and small shops (one block holds a larger store and a pink-coloured brick building at the centre). South of the road the street grid is turned about 50 degrees and covers the blocks 293 to 317: Bergen, Passaic, Essex, Neptune Place, Monmouth Parkway, Shoreland Terrace, Park Place, Sycamore and Cedar run across the sheet, with Union Place, Alpha Place, Laurel Place and Clinton at the lower right edge. Buildings are small frame dwellings, with names such as Acadia, Blue Bell, Belmont Villa, Chin Chin and Harlem Cottage. The sheet is marked 14 at left, 10 at the lower right and 16 at the foot, and a reference marked 2 at the upper right edge points to the Ideal Beach inset on sheet 2.
notes: Sea Breeze Avenue is now Seabreeze Avenue; Raritan Avenue is now Ideal Avenue; Bergen, Passaic and Essex are now Bergen Street, Passaic Street and Essex Street; Sycamore and Cedar are now Sycamore Avenue and Cedar Avenue.
Port Monmouth & Keansburg Road is now Port Monmouth Road.
Cedar Avenue and Cruse Place lay 8 to 10 m from their modern nodes and four such junctions were rejected, so the modern Cedar Avenue may have been realigned.
An AV. stands apart from the lettering Bay View at the right edge, and may belong to it.
Alpha Place is marked Arbitrary on the sheet.
100 ft. Ideal Beach: Board Parkway, Bayside Pkwy, Ocean, Hudson, Bray, Weehawken to Bay View Av; south grid (Bergen, Passaic, Essex, Cedar) turned about 50 deg.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16, titled East Keansburg and Port Monmouth, covers the eastern edge of the built-up shore district at 100 feet to an inch, from Cedar and Laurel Place at the top to the creek and the Central Railroad of New Jersey at the bottom, and from Harbor Way at the left to Raynor and Clinton Avenues at the right. The upper part is a regular grid of blocks 318 to 326 between Ocean Avenue, Monmouth Parkway, Shoreland Terrace, Hudson Avenue and Bray Avenue, mostly laid out in narrow lots with only scattered dwellings. Below it the streets turn and run in long diagonal blocks (Thompson, Kentucky, Dakota, Carter and Day Avenues, with Smith Place, Lester Place, Lovejoy, Nevada, Oregon and Columbia Avenues), more densely built with small frame houses, a fire department building, a cement block factory, a day house and a boarding house at Reiss Villa. A very large open tract, 422, with a compass rose, fills the left edge, and tracts 404 and 405 hold a few scattered buildings beside Harbor Way. The railroad crosses the lower half diagonally, with the Ohio, Jersey and Oregon Avenue blocks 427, 438 and 439 to its south-west and Iowa, Utah and Idaho Avenues, with blocks 452 to 455, to its south-east, ending at Pews Creek. The upper right carries the title block, a note on the scale and a small inset of Prospect and Clinton Avenues. The sheet joins sheet 15 at the top, 10 at the right and 17 at the lower right.
notes: Cedar, Linden, Pine and Centre are now Cedar Avenue, Linden Avenue and Linden Street, Pine Street and Center Avenue; Columbia Avenue is now Columbia Way; Hudson Avenue and Bray Avenue keep their names.
The street lettered Pine on the west half corresponds to modern Taylor Avenue.

Seven junctions were 7 to 14 m from their modern nodes and were rejected, among them Cedar Avenue / Hudson Avenue, Carter Avenue / Center Avenue, both Lovejoy Avenue junctions and Bray Avenue / Linden Street.
Ohio, Jersey, Iowa, Utah and Idaho Avenues were not used as control; they lie beside the railroad or in the unbuilt south end.
The Central Railroad of New Jersey is lettered along the diagonal rail corridor; it is abandoned and gave no control.
100 ft. East Keansburg: Cedar to Thompson/Kentucky/Dakota/Carter, railroad, Iowa/Utah/Idaho Avs, Pews Creek; southern third without control points.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 shows Port Monmouth at 100 feet to an inch, south of Pews Creek, which runs along the top of the sheet. Most of it is a large subdivision of long diagonal blocks, numbered 456 to 485, laid out in narrow lots with lot numbers written in each. The blocks run between Delaware, Texas, Montana, Illinois, Michigan, York, Carolina and Georgia Avenues, crossed by Vermont and Virginia Avenues, and are bounded on the east by Jersey Avenue with the street railway right of way beside it. Very few lots are built on: scattered one-storey frame dwellings and a hollow tile dwelling on Texas Avenue. East of Jersey Avenue the Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the sheet diagonally from Pews Creek to the lower right. Beyond it, around 2nd Avenue, Coe Place, Central Avenue and 1st Avenue, are a cement block manufactory, a dwelling drawn from plans and a few houses, with large empty tracts 461, 462, 469, 470 and 482, and Bray Landing Road along the east edge. Along the bottom, Monmouth Avenue and Harmony Avenue run across the sheet with a row of small lots, an auto repair shop of concrete block, a pool room and the Port Monmouth School, heated by steam and lit by electricity, near the railroad. Rex, marked arbitrary, and a street marked not named run between Georgia and Monmouth Avenues, and Walnut crosses Harmony Avenue at the bottom.
notes: Jersey Avenue and the street railway right of way are now NJ 36; NJ 36 was left out of the control because its junctions lie about 10 m from the drawn street.
Monmouth Avenue is now Wood Avenue; Harmony Avenue is now Main Street; Bray Landing Road is now Bray Avenue.
The Central Railroad of New Jersey line is abandoned.
A dwelling in block 468 is marked as drawn from plans.
A street is lettered "Not Named" on the sheet.
100 ft. Port Monmouth: Delaware, Texas, Virginia, Montana, Michigan, Carolina, Main, Port Monmouth Rd, railroad, Pews Creek.
